## Executive summary

This project builds a reproducible forecasting pipeline for daily Chicago
Transit Authority (CTA) system-wide bus, rail, and combined ridership. The
Python machine-learning evaluation compares Random Forest and XGBoost on a
chronologically held-out 10-week test period. Random Forest achieved the
lowest RMSE among those two tested machine-learning models for all three
modes. These results do not include the statistical baselines or optional
LSTM experiment, so they do not establish that Random Forest is the best
model across every approach.

## Problem and scope

The project forecasts next-day ridership separately for bus, rail, and
combined boardings. Reliable demand estimates can help transit planners
understand recent demand patterns and support planning discussions.
Forecasts are system-wide by mode; they are not route- or station-level
predictions.

## Data

The input is the CTA's [Ridership – Daily Boarding Totals dataset](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/CTA-Ridership-Daily-Boarding-Totals/6iiy-9s97)
from the Chicago Data Portal. The processed snapshot used for the reported
metrics covers **2001-01-01 through 2026-06-30**. Each source date is
reshaped into bus, rail, and total observations. Missing calendar dates are
represented explicitly; missing targets are excluded from model features.
Potential outliers are flagged for inspection rather than automatically
removed.

## Method

The feature pipeline creates lags of 1, 2, and 7 days; 7-, 14-, and
28-day rolling means and standard deviations; calendar and cyclical date
features; and a United States/Illinois holiday indicator. Lag and rolling
features use prior observations only.

Data is split chronologically rather than randomly. The last 10 weeks are
held out for testing, with the preceding 6 weeks used as validation for
the Python machine-learning workflow. Random Forest and XGBoost
hyperparameters are selected with `TimeSeriesSplit`. The test window for
the reported snapshot is **2026-04-22 through 2026-06-30**.

## Machine-learning results

| Mode | Best of evaluated ML models | MAE (rides) | RMSE (rides) | MAPE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Bus | Random Forest | 26,705.9 | 34,375.5 | 4.81% |
| Rail | Random Forest | 20,009.8 | 27,254.8 | 5.18% |
| Total | Random Forest | 46,210.5 | 59,673.3 | 4.87% |

The values are from [`ml_metrics.csv`](ml_metrics.csv). Random Forest
outperformed XGBoost by RMSE for each mode in this saved evaluation.
These results are tied to this data snapshot and holdout window; they are
not a guarantee of future accuracy. The statistical baseline notebook and
optional LSTM script are part of the repository, but their scores are not
included in this table.

## Dashboard

The Streamlit dashboard displays historical actual-versus-predicted
ridership and iterative short-horizon forecasts for the available trained
Random Forest and XGBoost models. Its widening forecast band is a
heuristic based on held-out RMSE, not a calibrated prediction interval.
The optional LSTM uses a different input format and is not served by the
dashboard.

## Limitations and next steps

- The dataset is system-wide, not route- or station-level.
- The current model does not include weather, service disruptions,
  special events, or other external drivers of demand.
- The training history spans major structural changes, including the
  COVID-19 ridership disruption; historical patterns may not represent
  future service conditions.
- The RMSE-based dashboard band is illustrative and does not quantify
  calibrated forecast uncertainty.
- Run the R baseline notebook and optional LSTM experiment on the same
  data snapshot before making a cross-family model-selection claim.
- Further work could add external covariates, evaluate per-route data,
  and use probabilistic forecasting methods.

## Reproducing the Python results

From the project root, install the core dependencies and run:

```bash
python -m src.data_prep
python -m src.features
python -m src.train_ml
python -m src.evaluate
```

See the project [README](../README.md) for environment setup and dashboard
instructions.
